prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1465; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for side impact collision at intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle entered the intersection against the signal. Police report requested. Claimant identified as driver of the other vehicle and reported concussion symptoms at scene. Claimant is represented by counsel; all communication to be routed through attorney's office.

Entry 2: Called claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and request medical authorization forms. Attorney's office stated they will provide signed HIPAA release within a few business days. Reviewed photos from insured's dashcam; impact appears to be to the driver's side rear quarter panel of claimant's vehicle. Vehicle inspection scheduled with independent appraiser.

Entry 3: Police report received. Responding officer cited the claimant for failure to yield at the intersection, with the insured's vehicle noted as having had a green signal. Witness statement from a pedestrian at the corner supports insured's account. Liability position tentatively set at seventy-five percent insured's favor pending further review. Reserves updated to reflect bodily injury exposure.

Entry 4: Received medical records from claimant's treating provider. Diagnosis includes concussion with post-concussive headaches and dizziness. Patient referred to neurology follow-up. Attorney's office sent demand package requesting policy limits settlement; demand under review by supervisor. Requested itemized billing and prior medical history for the past five years.

Entry 5: Reviewed demand package and medical file with claims supervisor. Recommended independent medical examination given ongoing symptom reports and treatment length. Sent IME request to counsel and awaiting response. Scheduled follow-up call with attorney's office to discuss documentation gaps. Claim remains open with liability and injury evaluation in progress.
